newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money edges up, gilt prices fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money edges up, gilt prices fall.

text.p: Indian call money rates moved up marginally to close on Wednesday at 4.5-4.75 percent while prices of government securities fell in dull trade, dealers said.
Call money opened in the 3.25 to 4.25 percent range and traded in the 4.0-4.5 percent range for most of Wednesday.

"There was a slight firming up of rates towards close of trade," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It was not very significant and we expect call rates to remain between four and five percent tomorrow."
Dealers said prices of government securities fell in limited trade. They said the marginal firming up of call money could have dissuaded players away from the securities market.
"Further many of the trading banks are busy finalising their positions ahead of the year-end," said a dealer. "There were very few deals today."
The 12.50 percent 2004 governemnt of India stock traded on Wednesday at 94.85 rupees against its last traded price of 94.90, dealers said.
Dealers said there were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial paper.
